Global Energy Monitor (2026). Global Iron and Steel Tracker, September 2026 (V1) release: plant-level data, iron unit data and steel unit data workbooks. https://globalenergymonitor.org/projects/global-iron-and-steel-tracker/ (accessed 2026-11-11).

HELD LOCALLY since 2026-11-11 (gem-data.zip, downloaded by the modeller). Three workbooks: plant-level data (plants, capacities by route, production 2019-2025), iron unit data (blast furnaces, DRI furnaces, relinings) and steel unit data (EAF, BOF, induction and open-hearth furnaces). Loaded by gem_extract.py: per-furnace nameplate capacity of the operating fleet for blast furnaces, gas-based shaft furnaces, BOFs and EAFs (scrap and reduced-iron charge split at 50% DRI+HBI+sponge iron), per-plant coke, sinter and pellet capacity, and plant-level 2024 capacity factors. Scope rule: Canada where three or more facilities report the value, else North America, else global (Brad 2026-11-11). Not loaded: induction and open-hearth furnaces (no archetype), coal-based and rotary-kiln DRI (no matching archetype), lifetimes and relining costs (_other-values). The Canadian roster with operating-capacity shares (_canada-stock.csv) is for calibrating CIMS technology shares later, not loaded. Traps: percentages of the EAF charge are printed as fractions (0-1); Cleveland-Cliffs Lake Erie's 2024 output is printed under 'EAF steel production' although the plant has no EAF (left out by the capacity match); Algoma's blast furnaces and BOFs are shown retired (EAF transition, 2025-2026); capacities printed 'unknown' or '>0' are not numbers and are skipped.
